narrative.overview: Every answer is a notebook entry that carries its evidence (the sources it cites, where they live, and how they were reached), and the interface recedes so that record can be read and checked.
keyCharacteristics: Three surface steps, depth by lightness, never by shadow.
Amber means the person; blue means the system. Never swapped.
Mono only for system-measured values: code, paths, line ranges, ids, counts, model names.
Show the code, not a picture of it: the right pane opens on the cited lines.
One filled primary action per view; everything else outlined or typographic.
Paper is the default colourway; graphite is the same tokens re-derived for dark, chosen in Settings or following the system.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Amber is the operator and blue is the readout, in every colourway. An amber citation or a blue Ask button is the system lying about who said what. Amber marks only the person's own state: their questions, the Ask button, the open repository tab, the keyboard focus ring. When the system points at something (a source row it opens, a node it pulses), that highlight is Readout Blue.

rules.name: The Signal Budget Rule
rules.body: Amber covers under 5% of any viewport. Its rarity is how the eye finds the next action.

rules.name: The Who-Wrote-It Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for what the system measured or the code contains. A label, heading or button in mono is costume.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 and 500 only. Hierarchy past that comes from size, colour and the surface a line sits on.

rules.name: The No-Lamp Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows, blooms or casts a shadow. If something needs to stand forward, it moves one lightness step.

dos: **Do** keep amber for the person and blue for the system in every new component and in both colourways.
**Do** set code, paths, line ranges, ids, counts and model names in the measured mono with tabular figures; set everything else in Host Grotesk.
**Do** separate panels that belong together with 1px hairlines on one surface, and step lightness for depth.
**Do** give every control all its states: hover, instant 2px focus ring, pressed, disabled (opacity, cursor and attribute together), loading, error.
**Do** key anything that refers to retrieved code like the graph: filled and ringed when the answer cites it, hollow when it was only retrieved, and label it with its S-number.
**Do** keep the graph's labels at 12px or more on screen: the fit stops zooming out where they would shrink, and labels that can't hold that size give way to the answer's.
donts: **Don't** add shadows, glows or gradients to any surface.
**Don't** use mono for labels, headings or buttons.
**Don't** put a second filled button beside the primary.
**Don't** join meta with middle dots or decorate labels with coloured dots; use columns, rules or separate elements.
**Don't** set labels in tracked capitals; labels are sentence case at 0.875rem, untracked.
**Don't** animate width, height or position; only transform and opacity, with a reduced-motion fallback.
